body.purpose: Default text size for tables, cards, forms.

label.purpose: Form labels, badge text, counters, timestamps.

mono.purpose: Reference numbers and monetary amounts only.

shadows.name: floating-medium
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus, select menus, popovers at rest.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action on a screen (e.g. + Nouveau contrat).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #102660; color: #f8fafc; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, #102660, black 10%); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(16,38,96,0.35); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: #f8fafc; color: #020817; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #e2e8f0; }

components.name: Status Badge (Active)
components.description: Pill badge for 'fine / active' status meaning (available billboard, active contract, paid invoice).
components.css: .ds-badge-active { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #d1fae5; color: #047857; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Status Badge (Needs Attention)
components.description: Pill badge for 'needs attention soon' status meaning (expiring contract, invoice nearing its relance deadline).
components.css: .ds-badge-alert { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #ffedd5; color: #c2410c; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat resting surface: tonal ring, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; color: #020817; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(2,8,23,0.1); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-card-sub { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #64748b; margin-top: 2px; }

components.name: Kanban Card
components.description: Signature component: status-colored left accent bar, bold reference title, muted subtitle, separate face/date elements (never one wrapping badge).

components.css: .ds-kanban-card { display: flex; background: #ffffff; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(2,8,23,0.1); overflow: hidden; } .ds-kanban-accent { width: 4px; background: #1d4ed8; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-kanban-body { padding: 12px; flex: 1; min-width: 0; } .ds-kanban-title { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; color: #020817; } .ds-kanban-sub { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #64748b; margin-top: 2px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-kanban-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin-top: 8px; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #64748b; } .ds-kanban-face { display: inline-flex; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 6px; background: #f1f5f9; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Vertical rail item; active state is a left accent bar plus a faint navy tint, never a full navy fill.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 10px; color: #64748b; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-item--active { color: #102660; background: rgba(16,38,96,0.05); box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 0 #102660; }

narrative.overview:
RNA Panneau is the screen a small team stares at every day to keep a billboard park under control: which faces are occupied, which contracts are about to lapse, which invoices are unpaid. The system is not selling anything to anyone — it exists so nothing slips through. That makes the right posture a control room, not a storefront: calm, authoritative, built for fast triage rather than persuasion. Deep navy carries the authority (used sparingly — an accent for actions and identity, not a backdrop), while the real workhorse is a disciplined status-color vocabulary that lets a Comptable glance at a column of cards and immediately know what's fine and what's bleeding money.

The system is currently under-designed relative to this ambition: components exist (Card, Badge, Button, Select, Dropdown, Popover, Tooltip) but have been assembled without a consistent rhythm, several screens still show default/cramped spacing, and status colors were added incrementally without a documented vocabulary. This file exists to fix that going forward — every new surface should read as the same disciplined operations tool, not a new experiment.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default; elevation reserved for things that float above the page (menus, popovers, dialogs), never for resting content.
One accent color (navy) used deliberately and rarely; status colors carry the day-to-day information load.
Dense, scannable layouts — this is a tool used for hours a day by 2-3 people, not a marketing surface.

rules.name: The Rare Navy Rule
rules.body: Control Navy appears only on the primary action of a screen and on active-state indicators (active nav link, focused input, selected tab). It never fills a whole card or section.

rules.name: The One Status Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Every status badge in the product must map to one of the five status colors by meaning (fine / in-progress / needs-attention / settled / wrong), not by picking a color that merely looks nice. A new status value gets assigned to the closest existing meaning before a sixth color is considered.

rules.name: The Data-Over-Decoration Rule
rules.body: There is no display/hero type scale in this system. The largest text on any screen is a page's h1 at Title size or one step up.

rules.name: The No Dead Space Rule
rules.body: A layout with a fixed number of columns/sections must stretch its columns/tiles to fill the viewport on wide screens. Horizontal scroll is only acceptable when the viewport genuinely can't fit the minimum readable width per item.

rules.name: The Flat-Content, Lifted-Overlay Rule
rules.body: If it's part of the page's normal reading flow, it gets a tonal ring only, never a shadow. If it floats above the page and can be dismissed by clicking outside it, it gets a shadow.

dos: Do reuse the five-color Status Vocabulary for any new status concept by mapping it to the closest existing meaning first.
Do stretch fixed-count layouts (Kanban columns, KPI tile rows) to fill the available width on desktop monitors.
Do use Control Navy sparingly — one primary action, active nav state, focus rings.
Do keep resting surfaces flat (tonal ring, no shadow); reserve shadows for floating/dismissible layers.
donts: Don't introduce a new status color without first checking whether it maps to an existing one of the five vocabulary meanings.
Don't add hover-shadows or lift effects to cards/rows to signal 'interactive' — use a background tint or border-color shift instead.
Don't combine two different pieces of information into one wrapping badge/pill — give each its own short element instead.
Don't use font-heading — it's referenced in one legacy component but no such font family is actually defined; either define it properly or remove the class.
